title: Types of AI: narrow, general and super
summary: ANI, AGI and ASI with their key traits and the professor's examples.

chunks.heading: Narrow AI (ANI): one task, done well
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck splits AI into three types. The first is **Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI)**, also called **Weak AI**.

**Key trait:** it is **task-specific** and **common**. It is built for one job and that is all it does.

**Examples from the slide:** **Netflix** recommendations, **Siri**, **Alexa** and **Face ID**. Each is clever at one thing only.
chunks.exam_line: Narrow AI (ANI) is task-specific and common, e.g. Netflix, Siri, Alexa, Face ID.

chunks.heading: General AI (AGI): learning across domains
chunks.explanation_md:
The second type is **Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)**.

**Key trait:** it **learns across domains**, not just one task.

**Examples on this deck's table:** **ChatGPT**, **IBM Watson** and **Google Gemini**. The diagram also shows **IBM Watson** and **OpenAI GPT-3** and says: *"We are halfway into successfully implementing this phase."*

Remember this is how this deck classifies these tools. In the exam, quote the slide's examples.

chunks.explanation_md:

questions.stem: Differentiate between Narrow AI, General AI and Super AI on key traits and examples.
questions.model_answer_md:
The session 2 slides divide AI into **three types**, from today's single-task tools to an imagined future AI.

**1. Narrow AI (ANI)**
- Also called **Weak AI**.
- **Key traits:** **task-specific** and **common**; built for one job only.
- **Examples:** **Netflix, Siri, Alexa, Face ID**.

**2. General AI (AGI)**
- **Key trait:** **learns across domains** instead of one task.
- **Examples in the table:** **ChatGPT, IBM Watson, Google Gemini**; the diagram also shows **OpenAI GPT-3**.
- **Status:** *We are halfway into successfully implementing this phase.*

**3. Super AI (ASI)**
- **Key trait:** **beyond human capability**.
- **Example:** none; it is **theoretical, future sci-fi robotics**.
- **Diagram line:** *Imagined how the world would be if machines occupy it.*

| Basis | ANI | AGI | ASI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Other name or status | Weak AI | Halfway implemented | Theoretical |
| Key trait | Task-specific, common | Learns across domains | Beyond human capability |
| Examples | Netflix, Siri, Alexa, Face ID | ChatGPT, IBM Watson, Google Gemini | Future sci-fi robotics |

**Reading the three together:** the types move from narrow to broad to beyond human. ANI is already everywhere, AGI is described as partly achieved, and ASI is only imagined.

**Conclusion:** for the exam, quote the deck's own table: ANI is task-specific (Siri), AGI learns across domains (ChatGPT) and ASI is beyond human capability (still theoretical).

questions.stem: Case: A company uses recommendations like Netflix for customers, Alexa for voice commands and ChatGPT for drafting reports. (a) Classify each tool by type of AI as per the slides. (b) Explain the trait that puts it there. (c) Explain why none of them is Super AI.
questions.model_answer_md:
The Types of AI table on slide 7 gives each type a key trait and named examples, so the company's tools can be matched directly.

**(a) and (b) Classification with reason**
- **Netflix recommendations: Narrow AI (ANI).** Netflix is a named ANI example. It is **task-specific**: it only recommends content. ANI is also called **Weak AI** and is **common**.
- **Alexa: Narrow AI (ANI).** Alexa is listed with Siri and Face ID under ANI. It handles one kind of job, voice commands.
- **ChatGPT: General AI (AGI).** The table lists ChatGPT, with **IBM Watson** and **Google Gemini**, under AGI because it **learns across domains**; drafting reports is only one of many things it can do. The diagram adds that *we are halfway into successfully implementing this phase*.

**(c) Why none is Super AI**
- ASI is **beyond human capability**.
- The table calls it **theoretical, future sci-fi robotics**, and the diagram says it is *imagined how the world would be if machines occupy it*.
- All three tools work within human-level tasks, so none qualifies.

**Conclusion:** the company runs two Narrow AI tools (Netflix recommendations, Alexa) and one General AI tool (ChatGPT), as this deck classifies them; Super AI does not exist yet.
